[discussion] Any video games that weren't that bad on their own but started bad/abused trends in gaming?

Might catch hell for this one, but I'd say AC started it's own bad trend. The series became a victim of its own success. I wasn't crazy about the first one, but loved the next couple. After that they just became unplayable to me because of the repetitive and grinding nature. Now, they just pump out broken games, announcing a new edition practically before the latest one is even released. The thought of playing one gives me heartburn. I keep trying to like them. I keep giving them chance after chance. But, they keep just giving me sadness. Nothing but sadness.
But has this affected only Assassin's creed franchise or has it leaked to other games as well?

I would say that the "trend" of putting out new games routinely, not because they are needed (or even wanted), but because the studio wants to just keep sucking as much cash out of the fanbase as possible, and in doing this completely diluting anything original or even mildly entertaining in the franchise, is not a result of AC, but I felt like bitching about it. COD has done it for years, but I don't think anyone would consider that franchise to be "original" anymore really. AC took something cool and original, and made it suck. But that's just my opinion.

I totally agree. I don't understand the love for AC series, it's just repetitive to hell. Thing is Ubisoft has taken the same formula and applied it to all their other games, Far Cry, Watchdogs. Unlock tower -> Do a bunch of side quests -> main mission -> repeat.

I get that other games kinda use the same formula (Saints Row), which is fine. It's just Ubisoft make their games so predictable that there's nothing to draw you into the game.
A lot of ubisoft games (far cry 3, 4, watch dogs) have pretty similar structure, so the series has definitely lead to a bit of internal homogenization in ubisoft's action adventure titles.

I loved the first one. Sure it needed some improvement, but the series has gone way downhill. Now you play as a war machine with personal motives, not an assassin who follows some kind of... oh, I don't know... a creed?

Ubisoft has tried to make content-heavy open world games in the same vein as what Rockstar and Bethesda do. The difference is that even with all their side content, Rockstar and Bethesda's main storylines are still interesting and memorable while Ubisoft's are boring as shit. I just finished AC Rogue a couple weeks ago and can barely remember any details from the story, same for Far Cry 4. I just remember Pagan Min was a dick and Amita whined a lot.

It's just the same thing again and again, just with a different skin. I mean, I did enjoy Far Cry 4, but mostly it was because I liked flying around on the helicopter and collecting animal skins. The actual missions I found to get a bit boring. AC has taken that to a new level for me. I would be happy as hell if I never had to do another "stealth/follow" mission, or "deliver this message to the other side of the map" in any game ever again.
If I was going to play it for the first time, which one would you recommend I get? I would usually just get the first (chronological etc.) but I often hear it's not the best. What do you think?

If I remember correctly, the first one is missing a few things that became essential later on in the series. The climbing is better in two. Combat added being able to throw dirt in the faces of people. I guess 1 is a decent game, but if you're going to play it, I'd play it first or else you will feel like something has been taken away from you. Plus AC2 gives us Ezio!
Maybe I'll check out 2. I don't have huge amounts of time for gaming these days so I'm looking for the best Assassins Creed experience.

What about...Call of Duty series, especially Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare? This was detrimental to level designs and over-reliance of spectacles in first-person shooters for years to come. I think the franchise also pulled Medal of Honor to the ground with MoH trying to emulate its success. Progression-based multiplayer system also meant a lot of grinding in many games.

COD 4 is still my favorite in the franchise. The level design was fantastic and the original kill streaks make sense. No incentives to camp for 25 kills, aside from bragging rights. Also the campaign was stellar. Slowly and then rapidly went downhill after that.
That's what I meant...started trends and weren't bad on their own but then were abused not only within but also outside the franchises.
I wasn't disagreeing with you. Only adding my opinion.

COD 4 was also the last in the franchise to have private servers. Now it's all hosted on people's consoles / central servers (for pc), which sucks. COD 4 was the last good one for a lot of reasons. It had its issues, but those problems exploded in later games.

Kill streak rewards + regenerative health are just fundamentally dumb. Suppressed weapons outside of hardcore mode are totally useless. Knife was always hilariously OP. Then they gave you infinite sprint as a perk and it was like free kills. Just run and stab, run and stab. Things may have changed, I don't know, I gave up on the whole franchise. Single player turned to crap and the game design for multiplayer was a joke.
World of Warcraft and the same-price-as-a-full-game-but-you-need-all-the-previous-expansions-to-use expansion. Maybe there were games that did it before WoW, but I couldn't say what they are.

At lease WoW stopped that by now.
Imagine how expensive it would be to get all expansions separately these days.
I think they only reason they bundle the old expansions together is because otherwise they'd never get any new players.

Arkham Origins. Just like Arkham Knight, the release was kind of shitty, but it was a good game if you could look beyond all the things that were wrong.

But then WB Montreal said they would spend zero time fixing any bugs that weren't game breaking and would instead focus all their attention on putting out the DLC for the game.

And that's why to this day the Crossfire support is absolutely terrible (playing it now and I get 7 fps during cutscenes and can't fast travel because it loads infinitely, but I can't disable Crossfire because then I only get ~30 fps during gameplay.)

Plus the gliding glitch (which also exists in Arkham Knight) has been in Origins since release day and will never be fixed.

It didn't start the trend of focusing on getting out DLC (which turned out to be terrible for the cost of the season pass, by the way) over fixing the game, but it abused it so bad that the police wouldn't need a witness statement from the victim to file charges.

Well, World of Warcraft ruined MMORPGs, kind of.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nvK8fua6O64

Mario Kart. It spawned a whole crap load of bad cart racers in the '90s.

Wii Sports. It basically set a bar early that the Wii was only good for mini-games and flooded the market with horrible mini-game based party games.
Resident Evil 4. Fantastic game, but it really crystallized the transformation of the big-budget horror genre into the big-budget action genre.

Oblivion and DLC. Particularly DLC that could/should have been part of the core game.

Additionally, Oblivion and graphic/feature downgrades from E3 footage.

Oblivion as a whole made me much more wary of the gaming industry.
Minecraft pretty much single-handedly created the early access trend.
Pong which created lots of Pong clones rather than trying something more original?

I realize this is a rather broad generalization but I tend to think this happens with almost all popular releases going back decades.

Gears of War would be my primary example though - It popularized the third person cover system despite it being in other games previously.

Unfortunately, that meant almost every third person game released for the next few years afterwards felt the need to have some sort of rudimentary cover system even if the game didn't necessarily benefit from it - E.g., Resident Evil 5.

That's what happens when someone uses something without realizing why it was implemented in the first place.

Although did Starcraft: Ghost start this trend despite not being released?
